title: Cartwise Shopper Payouts Risk Rules — Account Freezes and Destination Changes
content:
These rules of the Payments Risk team govern when a Cartwise Shopper Payouts account is frozen, when a freeze is lifted, and how the payout destination is replaced.

## R1. Causes of a freeze

| Cause recorded as the freeze reason | What brings it about |
|---|---|
| Transfer returned | A deposit or cashout is sent back by the receiving bank or card. The returned amount is credited back to the balance and, where the plan freezes on a returned transfer, the account is frozen. |
| Negative balance | The balance is more negative than the plan's negative balance limit. |
| Fraud review | A fraud review is opened. |

## R2. Lifting a freeze

A freeze is lifted by the agent only when its cause is resolved on the records. Each cause is resolved as follows:

- Transfer returned: resolved once a new destination has been recorded after the date the account was frozen.
- Negative balance: resolved once the balance is at or above minus the plan's negative balance limit.
- Fraud review: resolved only by the review team. A fraud-review freeze is targeted for decision within the plan's freeze review time in business days.

The evidence is the payout account record itself — its status, its freeze reason, its freeze date, the time the destination was last changed and the balance — for the same payout account. A shopper's statement that a new card "has been added" is not a record of a new destination.

### Points of judgement (hypothetical plan with a negative balance limit of 25.00)

| Freeze reason | Record shows | Cause resolved? |
|---|---|---|
| Transfer returned | A new destination recorded after the freeze date | Yes |
| Transfer returned | No new destination recorded after the freeze date | No |
| Negative balance | Balance minus 25.00 | Yes (at the limit) |
| Negative balance | Balance minus 25.01 | No |
| Fraud review | Any | Only the review team decides |

## R3. Destination changes

A destination change is allowed at most the plan's number of destination changes per 30 days, counted as the shopper's confirmed destination-change requests on the account created in the rolling 30 calendar days ending at the present moment. A destination change is made only on the shopper's confirmed destination-change request, and it starts the plan's destination-change cooldown, during which instant cashouts are blocked.

## R4. Clause no longer in force

The former clause under which a returned amount was sent again in the next weekly sweep once a new destination was on file, on plans that re-send returned transfers, is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current basis and is not applied. The plan setting on re-sending returned transfers remains a figure of each plan.

superseded_clauses: A returned amount is sent again in the next weekly sweep once a new destination is on file where returned_transfer_resend is true.
